introduction.value: Test suite for the ChibiOS/SB sandbox interface. The suite is executed inside a sandbox running ChibiOS/RT on the sandbox port, it verifies the host services from the sandbox side and measures the cost of crossing the sandbox boundary.

description.value: This sequence reports configuration and version information about the sandbox environment.
Sandbox-related info are reported.
Prints the sandbox settings.
This sequence tests the basic host services available to the sandbox through fastcalls and syscalls.
Fastcall and syscall codes not assigned by the host are invoked, the host is expected to serve them as not implemented.
An unassigned fastcall code is invoked, CH_RET_ENOSYS is expected.

code.value: msg = sb_test_unassigned_fastcall(); test_assert(msg == CH_RET_ENOSYS, "unexpected fastcall result");

description.value: An unassigned syscall code is invoked, CH_RET_ENOSYS is expected.

code.value: msg = sb_test_unassigned_syscall(); test_assert(msg == CH_RET_ENOSYS, "unexpected syscall result");

description.value: The null fastcall and the null syscall are invoked, the host is expected to serve them successfully.
The null fastcall is invoked, CH_RET_SUCCESS is expected.

code.value: msg = sbNopFastcall(); test_assert(msg == CH_RET_SUCCESS, "unexpected fastcall result");

description.value: The null syscall is invoked, CH_RET_SUCCESS is expected.

code.value: msg = sbNopSyscall(); test_assert(msg == CH_RET_SUCCESS, "unexpected syscall result");

description.value: The host system time services are tested.
The host system time frequency is read, a non-zero value is expected.

code.value: test_assert(sbGetFrequency() > 0U, "invalid frequency");

description.value: The sandbox sleeps for 10 milliseconds, the host system time is expected to advance within the allowed window.
This sequence tests the delivery of software-triggered VRQs to the sandbox, the per-VRQ enable and the global VRQ disable are tested.
The test VRQ is made pending while enabled, it is expected to be served on return from the triggering fastcall.
The test VRQ is enabled, no activation is expected without a pending request.

code.value: (void)__sb_vrq_seten(SB_TEST_VRQ_MASK); test_assert(sb_test_vrq_count == 0U, "spurious activation");

description.value: The test VRQ is made pending, the handler is expected to run once and the request to be cleared. The handler is expected to receive the VRQ number and no flags.
The test VRQ is made pending while individually disabled, it is expected to be served when enabled. A request withdrawn while disabled is expected to be discarded.
The test VRQ is made pending while disabled, no activation is expected and the request is expected to stay pending.
The test VRQ is enabled, the pending request is expected to be served on return from the enabling fastcall.
The test VRQ is disabled, made pending and then withdrawn, no activation is expected after enabling it again.
The test VRQ is made pending inside the kernel critical zone, which globally disables VRQs in the sandbox port, it is expected to be served when leaving the zone.
The test VRQ is enabled and made pending inside the critical zone, no activation is expected inside the zone.
The pending request is expected to have been served when leaving the critical zone.
A VRQ wait is performed while an enabled VRQ is pending and VRQs are globally disabled, the wait is expected to return without serving the request.
The test VRQ is enabled and made pending inside the critical zone then a VRQ wait is performed, the wait is expected to return without activations.
The pending request is expected to have been served when leaving the critical zone.

code.value: test_assert(sb_test_vrq_count == 1U, "not activated");

description.value:
This module implements a series of sandbox benchmarks. The benchmarks measure the cost of crossing the sandbox boundary, the numbers allow to discover performance regressions in the host and sandbox ports.
The performance is calculated by measuring the number of iterations after a second of continuous operations, the loop overhead is included.
The null fastcall is invoked in a continuous loop.
The fastcall is invoked continuously in a one-second time window.
Score is printed.
The host system time is read in a continuous loop.
The fastcall is invoked continuously in a one-second time window.
Score is printed.
The null syscall is invoked in a continuous loop, each iteration includes the check for pending VRQs on return from the syscall.
The syscall is invoked continuously in a one-second time window.
Score is printed.
The test VRQ is made pending in a continuous loop, each iteration includes the triggering fastcall, the delivery to the handler and the VRQ return fastcall.
The test VRQ is triggered continuously in a one-second time window, each trigger is expected to activate the handler once.
Score is printed.
The kernel critical zone is entered and left in a continuous loop, in the sandbox port each iteration includes the global VRQ disable and enable fastcalls.
The critical zone is entered and left continuously in a one-second time window.
Score is printed.
